newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge denies motion on racketeering law.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge denies motion on racketeering law.

text.p: A Florida judge Friday denied a request by tobacco companies to stop Florida from suing the industry under state anti-racketeering laws.
In a written ruling, Palm Beach County Circuit Judge Harold Cohen denied the industry's motion, a court clerk said.

Judge Cohen said at a preliminary hearing on Dec. 6 that he was inclined to let stand the civil claims filed under the state's Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organisations Act, which could mean more losses for cigarette makers.

The claims under the state RICO laws were added last month to Florida's existing lawsuit that seeks at least $1 billion for treating smokers' illnesses. Florida had said a victory under RICO could lead to triple damages against the tobacco companies.
The motion to throw out the claims under RICO was made by Philip Morris Cos. Inc., the world's largest cigarette maker, and other producers.
Officials at Philip Morris said they had not seen the judge's order and could not comment.
